text: Both Gold tables are loaded into Power BI and reconciled. Now it's time to build the first real page -- for Store Operations, the stakeholder this whole capstone started with, built on gold.daily_sales_summary.

Store Ops' question has never changed, from the Beginner project all the way through everything built in this course. How are my stores doing, day to day. That's a trend question, with a store-level lens, and gold.daily_sales_summary was built at exactly the grain that question needs -- one row per store_id per sale_date, holding total_sales and total_transactions.

This page needs three things, no more. A line chart of total_sales by sale_date -- a line, not a bar chart, because the question is about direction and change, and a line makes an upward or downward trend immediately visible in a way a bar chart of daily totals doesn't. A store_id slicer. And a total_transactions callout, a single prominent number for whatever store and date range is currently selected.

That slicer matters more than it looks. Store Ops doesn't ask about the whole chain in the abstract -- they ask about their stores, one at a time or a handful at a time. A slicer on store_id lets the exact same line chart answer how's store fourteen doing and how's store twenty-two doing, without building a separate page or a separate chart for every location.

The callout earns its spot too, even though it's just one number. Sales dollars and transaction count can tell different stories -- a high total_sales figure built from a handful of large transactions looks very different from the same number built from a lot of normal ones. The callout keeps that second number visible at a glance, instead of making Store Ops dig for it.

It would be easy to add more to this page -- a category breakdown, a month-over-month percent change, a cross-store comparison -- but none of that belongs here. Store Ops' actual question is a day-to-day, store-level trend, not a category question and not a cross-store comparison. That's a different ask, from a different stakeholder, answered by a different Gold table entirely -- which is exactly what the next lesson builds.
